name: Question 5
problem: Find the surface area of the part of the surface $y=\frac{4}{7}{x}^{7/4}+z$ whose projection onto the $xz$-plane is bounded by $z=\sqrt{x},$ $x=4,$ and the $x$-axis.
worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $y=f(x,z)$ with $(x,z)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂y}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂y}{∂z})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
y=\frac{4}{7}{x}^{7/4}+z,\,(x,z)\in D,
$$

where 

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 4,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{x}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071034/assets/0a4ed826b683e7e8d8ed3e05bcb75618e74314febcdda8ae31b09f379ca21c73.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂y}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{4}{7}{x}^{7/4}+z)={x}^{3/4}, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{4}{7}{x}^{7/4}+z)=1,\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂y}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂y}{∂z})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{({x}^{3/4})}^{2}+(1)^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{2+{x}^{3/2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}\sqrt{2+{x}^{3/2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}\sqrt{2+{x}^{3/2}}\cdot z\,{|}_{z=0}^{z=\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}\sqrt{2+{x}^{3/2}}\cdot \sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $u=2+{x}^{3/2},$ we get $\text{d}u=\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x.$ Also, the limits must be changed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & 0 & 4 \\ u & 2 & 10\end{aligned}
$$

 

Substituting these into our integral, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}\sqrt{2+{x}^{3/2}}\cdot \sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{2}^{10}\frac{2}{3}{u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{4}{9}{u}^{3/2}\,{|}_{2}^{10} \\  & =\frac{4}{9}({10}^{3/2}-{2}^{3/2}) \\  & =\frac{4}{9}(10\sqrt{10}-2\sqrt{2}) \\  & =\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{9}(5\sqrt{5}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

For a surface S defined by y=f(x,z) with (x,z)∈D, the surface area of S is given by

∬SdS=∬D1+(∂y∂x)2+(∂y∂z)2dA.

In this case, our surface is given by

y=47x7/4+z,(x,z)∈D,

where

D={(x,z):0≤x≤4,0≤z≤x},

as shown in the diagram below.

Now, since

∂y∂x=∂∂x(47x7/4+z)=x3/4,∂y∂z=∂∂z(47x7/4+z)=1,

the surface area is given by

∬SdS=∬D1+(∂y∂x)2+(∂y∂z)2dA=∬D1+(x3/4)2+(1)2dA=∬D2+x3/2dA=∫04∫0x2+x3/2dzdx=∫042+x3/2⋅z|z=0z=xdx=∫042+x3/2⋅xdx.
